goal: Define the dispatch parity product contract in Requirements.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/agent-conversation-dispatch/Requirements.md. Context: CL-06 in docs/functionality/CLIENT-DESKTOP.md already defines parity checks P-01..P-10 and conditional capabilities C-01..C-06, but there is no plan-local delivery contract stating which adapters, which lanes, and which user workflows this plan must make ready; the readiness reducer currently reports 0 ready with sendEnabled 0. Target: a Requirements.md that fixes REQ-ACD-001..006 (already tabled in Plan.md) into testable statements, names target users and workflows (direct conversation, orchestrated dispatch, mobile relay), defines scope and non-goals, and sets final acceptance targets per adapter tier (ready via official lane, blocked with recorded cause). Design Considerations: keep requirement labels stable and mapped 1:1 to the Plan.md table; parity is defined against observable native behavior (session continuity, event stream, cancel, on-disk history), not implementation internals. Design Value: every later node traces to a fixed contract, preventing implementation from silently redefining parity. Constraints & Risks: the user premise of unrestricted process access conflicts with CL-06.3; requirements must encode the official-lane boundary explicitly so no downstream node relitigates it.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md exists in the plan directory, restates REQ-ACD-001..006 as testable statements, and records users, workflows, scope, non-goals, and per-adapter acceptance targets.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Requirements.md present with REQ-ACD-001..006 testable statements, Target Users, Target Workflows, Scope/non-goals, and Adapter Acceptance Targets tiers.

acceptance_criteria.text: The official-lane compliance boundary from CL-06.3 is stated as a hard requirement with the exact prohibited techniques listed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Requirements.md present with REQ-ACD-001..006 testable statements, Target Users, Target Workflows, Scope/non-goals, and Adapter Acceptance Targets tiers.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: Official-Lane Boundary section states CL-06.3 hard requirement and lists prohibited techniques: ptrace, input injection, private-database mutation.

goal: Record per-adapter lane evidence and gap analysis in Evidence.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/agent-conversation-dispatch/Evidence.md. Context: crates/lico-client-native/resources/agent-conversation-drivers.json and agent-conversation-evidence.json record driver inventory and structural blockers, and crates/lico-client-native/src/platform/*_driver.rs implement history adapters, but nobody has consolidated which official runtime lane (CLI resume flags, ACP, app-server, stream-json, published attach protocol) each of the ten agents actually offers today, at which fidelity. Target: an Evidence.md that, per agent, cites the driver source file, the vendor-documented lane and its capabilities against P-01..P-10, the current reducer verdict from agent-conversation-readiness.json, and classifies the adapter as ready-candidate, lane-upgrade-candidate, or structurally blocked; include comparison notes on how each native tool exposes resume and streaming. Design Considerations: distinguish verified local observations from vendor documentation claims; evidence entries must carry file paths or command names, never invented capabilities. Design Value: implementation scope (which adapters the driver-parity node must upgrade) is locked by evidence instead of optimism. Constraints & Risks: agent CLIs change quickly; each evidence entry must record the tool version observed so stale evidence is detectable.

goal: Map every REQ-ACD label to concrete checks in Validation.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/agent-conversation-dispatch/Validation.md. Context: CL-06 already defines an evidence chain and the reducer enforces fail-closed readiness, so validation must plug into those mechanisms rather than inventing a parallel checklist. Target: a Validation.md that maps REQ-ACD-001..006 to named checks: Dart contract tests for the dispatch lane API, Rust driver tests per adapter, parity probe harness runs producing evidence artifacts, reducer gate assertions (sendEnabled stays 0 without evidence), UI widget tests for disclosure, and the architecture verifier; defines the end-to-end acceptance run and its pass condition before any implementation starts. Design Considerations: every check names the test file, harness command, or verifier it will exist as, and which node delivers it; checks that require locally installed agents are marked environment-dependent with a deterministic fixture fallback. Design Value: final validation becomes a mechanical run of this matrix instead of a judgment call. Constraints & Risks: overly environment-coupled checks would make the plan unverifiable on CI; each environment-dependent check needs its fixture-based counterpart stated here.

goal: Decide the dispatch module map, lane interfaces, and evidence flow in Architecture.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/agent-conversation-dispatch/Architecture.md plus empty interface scaffolds it prescribes. Context: today the only runtime lane is AgentCommandRunner.runCliWithStdin called from agent_conversation_service.dart, while drivers in crates/lico-client-native/src/platform/ diverge in resume and streaming semantics; orchestrated and relay callers reuse the same messaging actions. Target: an Architecture.md that fixes the module map with one responsibility per file: a Dart dispatch-lane contract (open/resume, send, stream, cancel, capabilities) in contracts/, one backend dispatch service implementing it over the sidecar RPC, Rust lane executors per protocol family (cli-resume, acp, app-server, stream-json) under the native crate, the parity probe harness as its own module, and the evidence artifact schema the reducer consumes; records dependency direction (UI -> application -> contracts <- backend <- native), interface signatures, and which parts stay pattern-free. Design Considerations: lane executors follow a strategy shape selected by driver metadata, because agents differ only in protocol family; the evidence artifact is a versioned JSON schema so the reducer contract is explicit; no new store — readiness stays in existing resources files. Design Value: implementation nodes can proceed in parallel on disjoint modules only if this map fixes the boundaries first. Constraints & Risks: the stdio RPC protocol (lico-client.stdio.v1) must gain lane methods without breaking existing callers; the architecture must state the RPC additions explicitly.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md records the module and file map, layer boundaries, dependency direction, lane executor strategy, and evidence artifact schema with rationale for each chosen pattern.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Architecture.md records module/file map, layer dependency direction, strategy pattern for lane executors, evidence schema, and pattern rationale.

acceptance_criteria.text: Interface contracts for the dispatch lane (Dart) and lane executors (Rust) are specified with method signatures and the stdio RPC additions named.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Dart AgentDispatchLane signatures and Rust executor surface specified; stdio RPC methods agent.conversation.open/send/stream/cancel/capabilities named under lico-client.stdio.v1.

acceptance_criteria.text: The document states which implementation nodes own which modules so parallel nodes touch disjoint files.

goal: Unify all conversation sending behind one Dart dispatch lane contract.
description: Scope: apps/desktop/lib/src/contracts/ (new dispatch lane contract file), apps/desktop/lib/src/backend/features/agents/services/agent_conversation_service.dart, apps/desktop/lib/src/application/features/agents/controller/agent_conversation_messaging_actions.dart and the orchestration/mobile-relay call sites that send messages. Context: sending currently hardcodes runCliWithStdin into one-shot `agent message send` calls — session creation is lazy (empty sessionId creates, non-empty resumes), there is no streaming or cancel surface, and the UI reconstructs state by full history readback after each send; orchestrated sends wrap prompts ad hoc on top of the same primitive. Target: one dispatch lane contract per the Architecture.md interface (open/resume, send, stream, cancel, capability discovery) implemented by the backend service over the sidecar RPC, consumed unchanged by direct, orchestrated, and relay callers; the legacy single-lane call shape is removed in the same pass. Design Considerations: the contract exposes lane capability metadata so callers can render what an agent supports instead of guessing; streaming surfaces the semantic event model already defined by agent_conversation_models.dart; cancel is a first-class method, not process kill from the UI layer. Design Value: parity work in the native crate becomes reachable by every caller at once, and no caller-specific protocol forks can reappear. Constraints & Risks: readiness gating in messaging actions must keep failing closed during the migration; the send gate check moves inside the lane entry point so no caller can bypass it.

acceptance_criteria.text: A dispatch lane contract exists in contracts/, the backend service implements it, and direct, orchestrated, and mobile-relay senders all call it; the previous runCliWithStdin call shape has no remaining callers in messaging paths.

goal: Implement per-protocol lane executors with native session continuity in the Rust sidecar.
description: Scope: crates/lico-client-native/src/platform/*_driver.rs, crates/lico-client-native/src/platform/runtime_adapters.rs, and the stdio RPC additions Architecture.md prescribed. Context: dispatch is already centralized — runtime_adapters::send_message matches a RuntimeAdapter enum into per-agent execute functions, and the ACP family (opencode, copilot, kilo-code, cursor, kimi-code, plus openclaw/hermes variants) shares one NDJSON state machine via AcpDriverSpec and execute_acp/probe_acp in opencode_driver.rs; codex-app-server and claude-code stream-json have their own machines; Claude Code fails closed on resume (claude_code_secure_resume_unavailable) and Cursor is blocked on exact_session_resume_unavailable as an evidence/policy verdict, not missing code. Target: extend the existing enum dispatch and shared protocol machines — not a parallel executor layer — so every lane family supports open-or-resume by native session id, lossless native event streaming into the semantic event model, cancel, and a per-agent capability matrix emitted into the drivers resource; lane-upgrade-candidate adapters from Evidence.md move onto their strongest official lane, structurally blocked adapters keep recorded causes. Design Considerations: keep the shared ACP machine as the single implementation for ACP agents and add family-level capabilities there once; introduce a shared executor interface only if Architecture.md justifies it over the current enum-plus-shared-function pattern; session identity mapping (LicoArc session to native session id) lives in one place; stderr and exit codes become structured errors, not swallowed output. Design Value: session continuity is the heart of parity — the native tool must later show the same conversation LicoArc drove. Constraints & Risks: CL-06.3 boundary applies — only official lanes; embedded drivers/readiness resources are validated at startup and drift causes hard parse failure, so resource updates ship with the code change; vendor CLI flag changes are detected by the harness rather than breaking silently; long-running streams must not block the sidecar event loop.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each protocol family (acp, app-server, stream-json, cli-resume) supports open-or-resume by native session id, lossless event mapping, cancel, and structured errors through the shared machines in runtime_adapters.rs and opencode_driver.rs — extended, not duplicated — with Rust tests per family using the existing fake-agent fixtures.

Each lane-upgrade-candidate adapter from Evidence.md runs on its strongest official lane and its capability matrix is emitted into the drivers resource; blocked adapters carry recorded structural causes.
cargo test passes and no executor uses ptrace, input injection, or private-database mutation.

goal: Build the parity probe harness and wire its evidence into the readiness reducer.
description: Scope: tools/scripts/client-acp-conversation-parity.mjs (the existing live A/B harness), tools/scripts/client-agent-conversation-parity-reducer.mjs, crates/lico-client-native/resources/agent-conversation-evidence.json, and agent-conversation-readiness.json. Context: the harness and deterministic reducer already exist — bidirectional native-to-Arc and Arc-to-native rounds, a three-consecutive-pass rule, a synthetic self-test wired into npm run client:verify:agent-conversation-parity — but the evidence manifest is empty (adapters: []) so all seven unblocked adapters sit at unverified, and CLIENT-DESKTOP.md notes the unified live runner across all lane families is not yet built. Target: converge on the existing harness as the single unified runner — extend it to cover every lane family delivered by the executors node and the full P-01..P-10 core checks through the real dispatch lane (open, send, stream, resume, cancel, then compare native on-disk history against the streamed record), write sanitized versioned evidence with tool versions and timestamps into agent-conversation-evidence.json, and let the existing reducer regenerate readiness; fixture-mode probes (existing fake-agent fixtures) cover CI where agents are absent. Design Considerations: no second harness — the migration-completion rule applies to verification tooling too; probes compare observable outcomes (history files the native tool itself reads, event sequences) rather than internal state; evidence stays diffable versioned JSON; the reducer remains a pure function of evidence inputs and keeps the binary-digest evidence binding (runtimeVersionDigest) enforced. Design Value: readiness flips become mechanical and reversible — a failing probe demotes an adapter automatically instead of leaving stale trust. Constraints & Risks: probes send real prompts to real agents, so they must use a dedicated throwaway workspace and redact machine-identifying content from evidence; harness runs must never mutate native stores beyond what the agent itself writes.

acceptance_criteria.text: The extended client-acp-conversation-parity.mjs harness runs P-01..P-10 probes through the real dispatch lane for every lane family per installed agent, writes versioned evidence into agent-conversation-evidence.json including tool version and timestamp, keeps its fixture/self-test mode for agent-absent environments, and no parallel harness exists.

The existing reducer derives ready strictly from current evidence with binary-digest binding intact; removing or invalidating an adapter's evidence returns it to unverified with sendEnabled 0, proven by the reducer contract tests.
Evidence artifacts contain no machine identity, secrets, or raw private paths; the hygiene check passes on generated evidence.

goal: Disclose per-agent parity state, capabilities, and blocked reasons in the conversation workspace.
description: Scope: apps/desktop/lib/src/frontend/features/agents/ui/agent_conversation_workspace.dart, agent_conversation_runtime_settings.dart, and the controller state that exposes readiness. Context: today a disabled send is silent or generic; Design.md requires process disclosure for agent conversations, and REQ-ACD-005 makes actionable gate messages a requirement; the dispatch lane and evidence chain now expose capability matrices and evidence age. Target: the workspace shows per-agent readiness state, capability matrix (what this agent supports through its lane), parity evidence age, and, when blocked, the recorded structural cause; every send-gate rejection renders the reducer's actual reason with the action that would unblock it. Design Considerations: reuse the existing readiness state flow from controller shell state rather than adding a second readiness fetch path; blocked-reason strings come from the drivers resource so UI copy never invents causes; keep disclosure inside existing workspace panels, no new page. Design Value: users can trust a green send button because the UI shows the evidence behind it, which is the product face of fail-closed parity. Constraints & Risks: disclosure must not leak local paths or machine identity from evidence artifacts; localized copy for gate reasons must stay in the existing localization flow.

acceptance_criteria.text: Widget tests prove the workspace renders readiness state, capability matrix, evidence age, and blocked structural cause per agent from reducer and drivers data.
Every send-gate rejection path renders the specific reducer reason and an unblock action; no generic disabled state remains.

goal: Run the Validation.md matrix end to end and prove REQ-ACD-001..006.
description: Scope: docs/plan/agent-conversation-dispatch/Validation.md execution, all delivered test suites, the parity harness, the reducer gates, and the client architecture verifier. Context: the validation matrix node defined every check and its pass condition before implementation; this node executes that matrix unchanged against the delivered code. Target: a recorded acceptance run showing Dart contract tests, Rust lane executor tests, harness runs against installed agents (or fixture mode where absent), reducer fail-closed assertions, disclosure widget tests, and the architecture verifier all passing, with results tied back to each REQ-ACD label; the client is rebuilt and opened per the repository delivery rule and any launch failure is reported. Design Considerations: run environment-dependent probes only against agents actually installed and record which tier each adapter reached (ready, blocked, unverified) as the delivered parity state. Design Value: the plan's claim — parity or explicitly blocked, never silent degradation — is proven by the same matrix defined at the start. Constraints & Risks: if any REQ label lacks a passing check, this node stays incomplete and the gap goes back to the owning implementation node; evidence in the report must be redacted per privacy rules.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every check in Validation.md runs with its result recorded against its REQ-ACD label, and all pass or carry an explicit blocked verdict with cause.
The final readiness report states each adapter's delivered tier with current evidence, and sendEnabled reflects only evidence-backed adapters.
The desktop client rebuilds and launches after delivery; build or launch failures are reported before handoff.
